resources.string: A security and privacy audit for Android. It reads your settings and explains them, and never changes anything by itself.
Droynis is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Lynis or CISOfy; Lynis was only the inspiration for a readable audit with a hardening score.

Every check that passed or failed counts, weighted by its severity. The score is the share of that weight you passed. Unknown and N/A results do not count either way, and neither do checks you muted.

A critical failure caps the score at 40: one critical gap undoes most other protections, so a high average would mislead. The dashboard also shows the score without the cap, so other fixes still count.

Two read-only permissions, granted once from a computer with adb, unlock checks that public Android APIs can\'t do. Droynis still never changes a setting.

Shizuku is an open-source app that gives other apps the rights adb has, without a computer once it runs. Through it Droynis starts a small shell that runs only a fixed list of read-only commands. It also runs every ADB-tier check, so the adb grants become optional.

1. Install Shizuku (open source, by RikkaApps).
2. Open Shizuku and start it: with Wireless debugging on Android 11 and later, or from a computer with adb. Shizuku shows each step.
3. Come back here and tap Allow access.
4. After every reboot, start Shizuku again.
For phones that are already rooted. Droynis will ask your root manager (such as Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) for a shell and run only a fixed list of read-only commands.
1. Open Droynis on the rooted phone.\n2. Allow root access when your root manager asks.\n3. Scan again.
Planned checks: files that even adb can\'t read, such as the list of computers trusted for USB debugging.
Rooting weakens Android\'s security model, so don\'t root a phone just to audit it. Root access (INTG-1050) stays a critical finding.

1. Turn on USB debugging and connect the phone to a computer with adb.\n2. Run the commands below.\n3. Tap Scan again. You can turn USB debugging off afterwards; the grants stay until you revoke them or reinstall.

Does a score of 100 mean my phone is safe?
No. Droynis checks the settings that public Android APIs can see. It cannot find malware, spyware hidden in system apps or tampered firmware. A high score means the basics are in place.

Android hides some settings from apps, and some vendors change or remove them. Droynis then says it does not know instead of guessing. Android 17, for example, can report USB debugging and developer options as off to every app.
Why does Droynis need to see all installed apps?
Since Android 11 apps see only a few other apps by default. Without the “query all packages” permission the app checks would miss most apps and pass falsely.
Can Droynis fix problems for me?
No, on purpose. It explains what to change and opens the right Settings screen, so you stay in control of every change.

Each check states the access it needs. Base checks work on any phone with no setup. ADB checks need two read-only permissions that you grant once from a computer (⋮ › Check catalog › ADB); until then they show as N/A and do not change the score. Shizuku runs the ADB checks without those grants and adds a few of its own, through a shell that runs only fixed read-only commands. Droynis reads only what its checks need, keeps nothing, and has no internet access to send it anywhere. A root tier comes later.
Does Droynis run in the background?
No. It scans only while it is open: no background services, notifications or wakelocks.
Can I leave out a check I can\'t fix?

Yes. Open the check and turn on “Mute this check”, or use the switch in the check catalog. A muted check still runs and shows its result, but the score, the counts and the issue lists leave it out, and reports list it as muted. Security patch age is the typical case: only the manufacturer can ship a newer patch.

No. Droynis is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Lynis or CISOfy. Lynis, an audit tool for Linux and Unix, only inspired the idea of a readable audit with a hardening score. Droynis shares no code with it.
